Then Allah explains what He will say to every one of these nations, in His saying: ﴿Then We will say: "Produce your proof"﴾, that is, your argument and evidence that I have partners. At that point they confess and are struck dumb, unable to establish proof. Therefore He said: ﴿Then they will know that the truth belongs to Allah﴾ in divinity, and that He alone has no partner, ﴿and what they used to fabricate will be lost to them﴾, that is, what they used to invent of falsehood in this world, namely that Allah has partners who deserve worship, will disappear, vanish and be gone.

Then Allah follows the account of the people of misguidance with the story of Qarun, because of what it contains of wondrous power and marvellous creation. He said: ﴿Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses﴾. *Qarun* is on the pattern of *fa'ul* and is a non-Arabic proper noun, which is not inflected because of its foreignness and its being a proper name. It is not an Arabic word derived from *qaranta* (to bind).

Al-Zajjaj said: if Qarun were derived from *qaranta al-shay'* (to join a thing), it would take nunation (tanwin).

Al-Nakha'i, Qatada and others said: he was the paternal cousin of Moses, namely Qarun son of Yashar son of Qahith son of Lawi son of Ya'qub, and Moses is the son of 'Imran son of Qahith.

Ibn Ishaq said: he was the paternal uncle of Moses, full brother of his father and mother; he made him a brother of 'Imran, and both were sons of Qahith. It is also said he was the maternal cousin of Moses. There was no one among the Children of Israel who knew the Torah better than him. He then became a hypocrite, as the Samiri did, and departed from obedience to Moses. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So he oppressed them﴾, that is, he exceeded the limit in arrogance and haughtiness towards them, went out against them, departed from Moses' obedience and disbelieved in Allah.

Al-Dahhak said: his oppression of the Children of Israel was his belittling them because of his abundance of wealth and children.

Qatada said: his oppression was attributing what Allah had given him of wealth to himself, due to his knowledge and cleverness.

It is also said that he was an official of Pharaoh over the Children of Israel, and he transgressed against them and wronged them. It is also said that his oppression was other than this, but that does not fit the meaning of the verse.

﴿And We gave him of the treasures﴾, the plural of *kanz* (treasure), which is wealth that is stored up.

'Ata' said: he came upon a treasure from the treasures of Joseph. It is also said that he practised *al-kimiya'* (alchemy).

In His saying ﴿Indeed, its keys﴾, *ma* is a relative pronoun whose clause is *inna* together with what is within its domain, and for this reason *inna* is pronounced with a kasra.

Al-Akhfash al-Saghir transmitted from the Kufans that they prohibited making the clause introduced by *inna* with a kasra and what is within its domain a relative clause of *alladhi*. He considered this an abomination on their part, because it occurs in the Mighty Book in this very place.

*Mafatih* is the plural of *miftah* with a kasra on the *mim*, which is that by which something is opened. It is also said that the intended meaning of *mafatih* is the storehouses, in which case its singular is *mafta*h with a fatha on the *mim*.

Al-Wahidi said: most of the exegetes hold that *mafatih* means the storehouses, as in His saying: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen﴾ (al-An'am 6:59). He said: this is the view chosen by al-Zajjaj, for he said: the more likely interpretation is that its keys are the storehouses of his wealth.

Others said: they are the plural of *miftah*, which is that by which a door is opened. This is the view of Qatada and Mujahid.

﴿Would bend the group of strong men﴾. This clause is the predicate of *inna*, and *inna* together with its subject and predicate forms the relative clause of *ma*. It is said: *na'a bi-hamlihi* means he rose up with it heavily laden; and *na'a bi-l-hamlu* means the load weighed him down. The meaning is that the burden of the keys weighs them down.

Abu 'Ubayda said: this is an inverted usage, and the meaning is: the group rises up with them, that is, stands up with them.

Abu Zayd said: *nu'tu bi-l-hamli* means that you rose up with the load. The poet said:

*"We found a successor, most wretched successor, a servant who, when he rises with the load, stands still."*

Al-Farra' said: the meaning of *tanu'u bi-l-'usbah* is that it inclines them with its weight, as one says: *yadhhabu bi-l-bu'si* and *yadhhabu al-bu's* (he takes away the misery), *dhahabtu bihi* and *adhhabtuhu* (I went with it and I made it go), *ji'tu bihi* and *aja'tuhu* (I brought it and I made it come), *nu'tu bihi* and *an'atuhu* (I raised it and I made it rise). Al-Nahhas chose this view, and many of the *salaf* (the earliest generations of Muslims) said likewise.

It is also said that it is derived from *al-na'y* (distance), but this is far-fetched.

Budayl ibn Maysara read *li-yanu'a* with a *ya'*, meaning: so that one of them, or the one mentioned, would bend under it. It was taken in this sense. The group (*'usbah*) is a company whose members support one another. It is said it is from three to ten; it is also said from ten to fifteen; it is said between ten and twenty; it is said from five to ten; it is said forty; it is said seventy; and it is said other than this.

﴿When his people said to him: "Do not exult"﴾. The adverbial clause is in the accusative governed by *tanu'u*. It is also said it is governed by *atayna-hu*, and also by *baghā*.

Abu Hayyan rejected both, on the ground that the giving and the transgression did not occur at that time.

Ibn Jarir said: it is connected to an elided verb, which is *udhkur* (remember), and the intended "his people" here are the believers from the Children of Israel.

Al-Farra' said: it is Moses, and it is a plural used for the singular. The meaning of "do not exult" is: do not be insolent or arrogant. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the exultant﴾, the insolent and arrogant, who do not thank Allah for what He has given them.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: do not exult in wealth, for one who exults in wealth does not fulfil its right. It is also said the meaning is: do not corrupt, as in the words of the poet:

*"If you do not cease to discharge a trust, and then bear another, the deposits will make you exult."*

That is: they will corrupt you. Al-Zajjaj said: *al-farihin* and *al-farihin* are equivalent. Al-Farra' said: *al-farihin* are those who are in a state of exultation, and *al-farihin* are those who will exult in the future.

Mujahid said: the meaning of "do not exult" is "do not transgress," and "Allah does not love the exultant" means the transgressors.

It is also said that it means: do not be miserly, for Allah does not love the miserly.

﴿And seek, in what Allah has given you, the Hereafter abode﴾, that is: seek, through the wealth Allah has given you, the Hereafter abode, so spend it in what pleases Allah, not in arrogance and transgression. It has been read as *wa-ittabi'* (and follow).

﴿And do not forget your share of this world﴾. The majority of exegetes said: this means that one should work in one's worldly life for the sake of the Hereafter, and a person's share is his lifespan and his righteous deeds.

Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is: do not forget to work for your Hereafter, because the reality of a person's share of this world is that through which he works for his Hereafter.

Al-Hasan and Qatada said: its meaning is: do not neglect your portion of your worldly life in enjoying what is lawful and seeking it. This is closer to the sense of the Qur'anic wording.

﴿And do good as Allah has done good to you﴾, that is, do good to the servants of Allah as Allah has done good to you by the blessings of this world with which He has favoured you. It is also said: obey Allah and worship Him as He has favoured you. This is supported by what is established in the *Sahihayn* (the two *Sahih* collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim) and others, that Gabriel asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about *ihsan* (excellence), and he said: "That you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, He sees you."

﴿And do not seek corruption in the earth﴾, that is, do not act in it with the disobedience of Allah. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the corrupters﴾ in the earth.

﴿He said: "I was only given it on knowledge I have"﴾. Qarun said this statement in reply to those who advised him with what has preceded. That is: I was only given the wealth I was given because of my knowledge. So his saying *'ala 'ilm* (on knowledge) is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause, and *'indi* (with me) is either an adverb of place for *ufitituhu* (I was given it), or a complement to *'ilm* (knowledge). This knowledge is what he made the cause of what he obtained of this world.

It is said: it is knowledge of the Torah. It is said: it is his knowledge of the ways of earning and trade. It is said: it is knowledge of the knowledge of treasures and hidden stores. It is said: it is the knowledge of alchemy. It is said: the meaning is that Allah gave me these treasures with knowledge from Him of my worthiness for them, because of the excellence of His knowledge of me.

Al-Zajjaj chose this view and rejected all others.

Then Allah refuted his statement, saying: ﴿Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him generations who were greater than him in strength and more abundant in accumulation?﴾ The *qurun* (generations) are the former nations. The meaning of "more abundant in accumulation" is: more abundant than him in gathering wealth. Had wealth or strength indicated excellence, Allah would not have destroyed them.

It is also said: *quwwah* (strength) refers to instruments, and *jam'* (accumulation) refers to helpers.

This statement is in the form of rebuke and reproach directed at Qarun, because he had read the Torah and knew the knowledge of the earlier generations and how Allah, the Glorified, destroyed them.

﴿And the guilty will not be asked about their sins﴾, that is, they will not be asked in a manner of seeking to be pleased, as in His saying: ﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends﴾ (al-Nahl 16:84; al-Rum 30:57), ﴿So they will not be among those who are made to make amends﴾ (Fussilat 41:24). They will only be asked in a manner of rebuke and reproach, as in His saying: ﴿By your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ (al-Hijr 15:92).

Mujahid said: the angels will not ask tomorrow about the guilty, because they will be recognised by their marks, for they will be gathered with black faces and blue eyes.

Qatada said: the guilty will not be asked about their sins because they are apparent and numerous, but they will enter the Fire.

It is also said: the guilty of this nation will not be asked about the sins of the former nations.

﴿So he went out to his people in his adornment.﴾ The *fa'* (فَ) is conjunctive, linking to "[He] said" (قالَ) earlier, with the intervening material being a parenthetical insertion (*i'tiraD*, an interjected clause). The phrase ﴿in his adornment﴾ (فِي زِينَتِهِ) is connected either to "went out" (خَرَجَ) or to an omitted verb, and it functions as a circumstantial qualifier (*hal*) of the subject of "went out."

The exegetes have transmitted various reports about the adornment in which he went out, but the meaning is that he went out in a display that dazzled everyone who saw it. For this reason, those who observed him wished that they too had the like of it, as God relates about them when He says: ﴿Those who desired the life of this world and its adornment said, "Would that we had the like of what Qarun was given! Indeed, he is possessed of great fortune."﴾ That is, a abundant share of worldly goods.

The exegetes differ regarding who these people were who spoke this statement. It has been said that they were believers of that time, and it has been said that they were a group of disbelievers.

﴿But those who had been given knowledge said﴾, and they were the rabbis (*ahbar*) of the Children of Israel, they said to those who had wished: ﴿Woe to you! The reward of God is better﴾, that is, God's reward in the Hereafter is better than what you wish for, ﴿for those who believe and do righteous deeds.﴾ So do not wish for the fleeting goods of this world, which do not endure. ﴿But none receives it except the patient﴾, that is, this word which the rabbis spoke. It has been said that the pronoun refers to the righteous deeds, and it has been said that it refers to Paradise. ﴿Except the steadfast﴾ in obedience to God, and those who restrain themselves from desires.

﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾. It is said: "The place sank (*khasafa*) and sinks (*yakhsifu*), sinking (*khusuufan*)": it went down into the earth. And "He caused the earth to swallow him (*khasafa bihi al-ard*), swallowing (*khasfan*)": that is, he disappeared into it. The meaning is that God, glorified is He, made him disappear and made his home disappear into the earth. ﴿So he had no company to help him against God, nor was he among those who could defend himself﴾: that is, he had no group who could ward this off from him, nor was he himself among those who could protect himself against the sinking that had befallen him.

﴿And those who had wished to be in his place yesterday began to say﴾, that is, in the recent past, ﴿"Ah! It is God who expands provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it. Had God not been gracious to us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us! Ah! The disbelievers will never prosper."﴾ That is, each of them said, regretting what had escaped from him of wishing.

An-Nahhas said: "The best that has been said about this is what al-Khalil, Sibawayh, Yunus and al-Kisa'i said: that the people became alert and said *way* (وَيْ). The one who regrets among the Arabs says *way* in the midst of his remorse." Al-Jawhari said: "*Way* (وَيْ) is an expression of wonder. It is also said *waykа* (وَيْكَ), and *way* may enter upon *ka'anna* (كَأنَّ), both the light and the heavy forms: *waykaʾanna Allah* (وَيْكَأنَّ اللَّهَ)." Al-Khalil said: "It is separated: you say *way*, then you begin and say *ka'anna*." Al-Farra' said: "It is a word of affirmation, like your saying: *Do you not see God's handiwork and His kindness?*" It has also been said: "It is a word of alerting, equivalent to *ala* (أَلا)." Qutrub said: "It is originally *wayka* (وَيْكَ), and its *lam* (لام) was dropped," and from it is the saying of 'Antarah:

*And indeed he has healed my soul and cured its ailment: the saying of the horsemen, "Wayka, 'Antar, advance!"*

Ibn al-A'rabi said: the meaning of *waykaʾanna Allah* is: "I know that God..." Al-Qutabi said: its meaning in the dialect of Himyar is "mercy." It has also been said: it means "Did you not see?" It is reported from al-Kisa'i that he said: it is an expression of grief.

﴿Had God not been gracious to us﴾ with His mercy and preserved us from the like of what Qarun had been upon, of insolence and transgression, and had not taken us to account for what had occurred from us of that wishing, ﴿He would have caused the earth to swallow us﴾ just as He caused it to swallow him.

Hafs read *la-khasafa* (لَخَسَفَ) with the active verb, while the rest read it in the passive. ﴿Ah! The disbelievers will never prosper﴾, that is, they will not attain any of their aims.

﴿That is the Last Abode﴾, that is, Paradise. The pointing to it is for the purpose of exalting it and magnifying its status, as if He said: "That which you have heard of and whose matter has reached you." ﴿We appoint it for those who do not desire exaltation in the earth﴾, that is, rising and arrogance over the believers, ﴿nor corruption﴾, that is, acting in disobedience to God, glorified is He. The mention of exaltation and corruption as indefinite nouns within a negative context indicates that both are general, covering everything to which the term "exaltation" or "corruption" applies, without restriction to any particular type. As for corruption, it is clear that no part of it is permitted, whatever it may be. As for exaltation, what is prohibited is that which is by way of arrogance toward others and haughtiness over people. Excluded from this is the pursuit of elevation in the truth and leadership in religion, nor the love of fine clothing, fine mount, or fine dwelling.

﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it﴾, and that is that God rewards him tenfold, up to seven hundredfold. ﴿And whoever brings an evil deed, those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed except according to what they used to do.﴾ That is, except the like of what they used to do; the genitive complement has been omitted and the complement after it has been put in its place. The explanation of the meaning of this verse has already been given in Surat al-Naml.

﴿Indeed, He who ordained the Qur'an upon you﴾. The exegetes said: that is, He revealed the Qur'an to you. Al-Zajjaj said: He imposed upon you the obligation to act in accordance with what the Qur'an requires, and the sense of the statement is: He imposed upon you the rulings and obligations of the Qur'an. ﴿Will surely bring you back to a return (*ma'ad*).﴾ The majority of exegetes said: that is, to Mecca.

Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Zuhri and al-Hasan said: the meaning is: "He will surely bring you back to the Day of Resurrection," and this is the choice of al-Zajjaj. It is said: "Between me and you is the *ma'ad*," that is, the Day of Resurrection, because people return (*ya'uduna*) in it alive.

Abu Malik and Abu Salih said: "He will surely bring you back to a return," that is, to Paradise. This was also said by Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and it is reported from Mujahid.

It has also been said: *ma'ad* means death. ﴿Say, "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance and who is in clear error."﴾ This is an answer to the disbelievers of Mecca when they said to the Prophet (ﷺ), "You are in error." The intended meaning of "who has come with guidance" is the Prophet (ﷺ), and "who is in clear error" refers to the polytheists. The more appropriate reading of the verse is that it is general: God, glorified is He, knows the condition of each of these two groups and will recompense each according to what it deserves of good or evil.

﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be cast to you﴾, that is, you did not expect that We would send you to the servants and reveal the Qur'an to you. It has also been said: you did not expect that the Book would be cast to you except by your being returned to your *ma'ad*. The exception in His words ﴿except as a mercy from your Lord﴾ is disjunctive (*munqati'*), that is, "but its being cast to you is a mercy from your Lord." It is also permissible for it to be connected (*muttasil*), by taking it according to the sense, as if it were said: "The Book was not cast to you except for the sake of mercy from your Lord." The first is preferable, and al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' affirmed it.

﴿So never be an aide to the disbelievers﴾, that is, a supporter for them. This contains an allusion to others among the community. It has also been said: the intended meaning is, do not be a supporter for them by flattering them.

﴿And let them not averted you from the signs of God after they have been revealed to you﴾, that is: O Muhammad, let not the disbelievers, their statements, their lies, and their harm, turn you away from reciting the signs of God and acting upon them after God has revealed them to you and they have been made obligatory upon you.

The majority read *yasuddannaka* (يَصُدَّنَّكَ) with a fathah on the *ya'* and a dammah on the *sad*, from *sadda, yasuddu*. 'Asim read it with a dammah on the *ya'* and a kasrah on the *sad*, from *asadda*, with the same meaning as *saddaha*. ﴿And call to your Lord﴾, that is, call people to God and to His oneness, to acting upon His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions. ﴿And do not be among the polytheists﴾. This also contains an allusion to others, as mentioned earlier, since he (ﷺ) would never be among the polytheists under any circumstances.

Likewise His words: ﴿And do not invoke with God another deity﴾, for it is an allusion to others.

Then He, glorified is He, singled Himself out and described Himself as enduring and everlasting, saying: ﴿There is no deity except Him. Everything will perish except His Face﴾, that is, except His Essence, of all things, whatever they may be.

Al-Zajjaj said: "*Wajhahu* (وَجْهَهُ) is in the accusative as an exception. Had it been outside the Qur'an, it would have been in the nominative, meaning: everything other than His face is perishing, as the poet said:

*And every brother, his brother will part from him, by the life of your father, except the two Pleiades (al-Farqadan)*

The meaning is: every brother other than the two Pleiades will be parted from by his brother. ***Lahu al-hukm*** (لَهُ الحُكْمُ): that is, the executing judgment; He decides what He wills and rules by what He desires, and to Him you will be returned at the Resurrection, so that He may recompense the good-doer for his goodness and the evildoer for his evil. There is no deity but Him, glorified and exalted is He.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿perpetual (*sarmadan*)﴾ that he said: "Continuous."

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him regarding ﴿and what they used to invent (*yaftarun*) will be lost to them﴾ on the Day of Resurrection that he said: "They used to lie in the world."

Ibn Abi Shaybah in *al-Musannaf*, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh reported from him as well regarding ﴿Indeed, Qarun was of the people of Moses﴾ that he said: "He was his paternal cousin, and he pursued knowledge until he gathered a body of knowledge. He continued in this matter until he rebelled against Moses and envied him. Moses said to him, 'God has commanded me to take the zakat.' He refused and said, 'Moses wants to eat up your wealth. He brought you prayer and brought you things, and you bore them. Will you bear giving him your wealth?' They said, 'We will not bear it. So what do you suggest?' He said to them, 'I suggest that we send to a prostitute among the prostitutes of the Children of Israel and send her to him, so that she accuses him of having wanted her for herself.' They sent to her and said, 'We will give you your reward on condition that you testify against Moses that he committed adultery with you.' She said, 'Yes.' Then Qarun came to Moses and said, 'Gather the Children of Israel and inform them of what your Lord has commanded you.' He said, 'Yes.' So he gathered them, and they said to him, 'What has your Lord commanded you?' He said, 'He commanded me that you worship God and associate nothing with Him, and that you maintain the ties of kinship, such and such.' And He commanded me that if someone commits adultery after being married, he should be stoned.' They said, 'Even if you are the one?' He said, 'Yes.' They said, 'You have committed adultery.' He said, 'I?' They sent for the woman, and she came. They said, 'What do you testify concerning Moses?' Moses said to her, 'I adjure you by God, speak the truth!' She said, 'As for when you adjure me by God, they called me and offered me a payment on condition that I accuse you with myself, while I testify that you are innocent and that you are the Messenger of God.' Moses fell down in prostration weeping. God revealed to him, 'What makes you weep? We have empowered you over the earth, so command it and it will obey you.' He raised his head and said, 'Seize them.' It seized them up to their ankles, and they began to say, 'O Moses, O Moses!' He said, 'Seize them.' It seized them up to their knees, and they began to say, 'O Moses, O Moses!' He said, 'Seize them.' It seized them up to their necks, and they began to say, 'O Moses, O Moses!' He said, 'Seize them.' It seized them and engulfed them. God revealed, 'O Moses, My servants asked you and humbled themselves before you, and you did not respond to them. By My might, had they called upon Me, I would have responded to them.'"

Ibn 'Abbas said: "That is His saying: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾. He was swallowed down into the lowest earth."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Khaythamah that he said: "The keys to the treasures of Qarun were made of hide, each key like a finger. Each key was for a separate treasure-house. When he rode, the keys were carried on seventy white-blazed mules."

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir reported from him: "I found in the Gospel that the mules bearing the keys to the treasuries of Qarun were white-blazed, and no key of them exceeded a finger in size, each key for a treasure."

I say: I have not found in the Gospel what Khaythamah mentioned.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿would weigh down with the band﴾ that he said: "It burdens." And Ibn al-Mundhir reported from him that he said: "The band (*'usbah*) of men of strength could not lift them." Ibn Jarir also reported from him: "The *'usbah* is forty men."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him also regarding His words ﴿Indeed, God does not love the exultant﴾ that he said: "The insolent (*maridin*)." And regarding His words ﴿And do not forget your share of the world﴾ he said: "That you work in it for your Hereafter."

Ibn Mardawayh reported from Aws ibn Aws al-Thaqafi, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His words ﴿So he went out to his people in his adornment﴾: "With four thousand mules."

Reports have been transmitted from a group of the Successors (*tabi'un*) concerning the statements explaining what he went out with to his people in adornment, but none of them is authentic as a hadith traced to the Prophet. Rather, they are from the reports of the People of the Book, as we have made clear to you more than once. I do not know the chain (*isnad*) of this hadith which Ibn Mardawayh traced to the Prophet, so whoever finds his book, let him examine it.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 28, verse 71–88 (part 3 of 3):

Al-Firyabi narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾. He said: He was made to sink into the lowest earth.

Al-Mahamili and al-Daylami, in Musnad al-Firdaws, narrated from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), regarding His saying: ﴿That is the abode of the Hereafter. We assign it to those who do not desire haughtiness upon the earth or corruption﴾. He said: "Arrogance upon the earth and taking by other than the truth."

A similar report is narrated from Muslim al-Bitin, Ibn Jurayj and ʿIkrimah.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Saʿid ibn Jubayr regarding ﴿who do not desire haughtiness upon the earth﴾: He said: Transgression upon the earth.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Hasan, who said: It is nobility and superiority in the eyes of those who hold authority over them.

I say: If that is for the sake of strengthening oneself through it in the cause of the truth, then it is one of the qualities of good, not one of the qualities of evil.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, who said: "Indeed, a man may love that the thong of his sandal be better than the thong of his companion's sandal, and so he enters into this verse: ﴿That is the abode of the Hereafter. We assign it to those who do not desire haughtiness upon the earth or corruption﴾."

Ibn Kathir, in his Tafsir, after mentioning this report from ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him), said: This is to be understood as referring to one who loves that out of pride, not merely for beautification; as for the latter, there is no harm in it, for it is established that "a man said: O Messenger of Allah, I love that my garment be fine and my sandal be fine. Is that from pride? He said: No. Indeed Allah is Beautiful and loves beauty."

Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn ʿAsakir narrated from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib that he said: This verse, namely ﴿That is the abode of the Hereafter﴾ etc., was revealed concerning people of justice and humility among the rulers, and among those with power from the rest of the people.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar report from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from ʿAdi ibn Hatim, who said: "When he entered upon the Prophet (ﷺ), he threw to him a cushion, but he sat on the ground and said: I bear witness that you do not seek haughtiness upon the earth or corruption. So he embraced Islam."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Dahhak.

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from ʿAli ibn al-Husayn ibn Waqid that His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, He who has ordained the Qur'an upon you﴾ — the verse — "was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at al-Juhfah when the Prophet (ﷺ) departed as an emigrant to Madinah."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated through several chains from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿Surely He who ordained the Qur'an upon you will return you to a place of return﴾. He said: To Makkah. Ibn Mardawayh added: "As He brought you out from it."

Al-Firyabi, ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri regarding ﴿will return you to a place of return﴾: He said: The Hereafter.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Bukhari in his Tarikh, Abu Yaʿla and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him also, regarding His saying: ﴿will return you to a place of return﴾: He said: Its return is Paradise; and in another wording: its return is its Hereafter.

al-Hakim in al-Tarikh and al-Daylami narrated from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, who said: ﴿will return you to a place of return﴾: Paradise.

Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar report from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him, who said: When the verse ﴿Everyone upon it will perish﴾ [al-Rahman: 26] was revealed, the angels said: The people of the earth have perished. When the verse ﴿Every soul will taste death﴾ [Al ʿImran: 185] was revealed, the angels said: Every soul has perished. When the verse ﴿Everything will perish except His Face﴾ was revealed, the angels said: The people of the heavens and the earth have perished.

ʿAbd ibn Humayd narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding ﴿Everything will perish except His Face﴾: He said: Except what is intended by His Face.

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (*Fath al-Qadir*) on Surah 28, verses 71–88 (part 1 of 3)**

Allah says: ﴿Say: "Tell me, if Allah made the night perpetual over you"﴾, meaning: inform me. *Sarmad* (perpetual, continuous) comes from *al-sard* (succession, continuity), and the *mim* is extra. Tarafa said:

*"By your life, my affair is not a cloud over you, neither my day nor my night is perpetually over you."*

It is also said that the *mim* is original, and its form is *fa'lal*, not *fa'mal*, and this is the more apparent view. Allah explains that He has prepared for them the means of livelihood so that they may give thanks for the blessing. If the age in which they live were a night that lasted until the Day of Resurrection, they would not be able to move about in it and seek what they must have of food, drink and clothing, which sustain life. Then He reminds them of His favour, saying: ﴿Who is a god other than Allah who could bring you light?﴾, meaning: is there among the gods you worship one that can lift this lasting darkness from you by means of *diya'* (light), that is, by a light in which you seek your livelihood, see what you need, have your fruits ripen, have your crops grow, and have your animals live? ﴿Will you not then listen?﴾, that is, listen with understanding, acceptance, reflection and contemplation.

Then, having finished reminding them of the favour of day, He reminds them of the favour of night, saying: ﴿Say: "Tell me, if Allah made the day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection"﴾, meaning: He made the whole age in which you live a day until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Who is a god other than Allah who could bring you a night in which you may rest?﴾, that is, in which you settle from weariness and fatigue and rest from the toil of seeking livelihood and earning. ﴿Will you not then see?﴾, that is, see this great benefit with the sight of one who takes heed and is awake, so that you may desist from what you are engaged in, namely the worship of other than Allah. When they acknowledge that none can do this except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, the proof is established against them and the doubtful arguments they cling to are invalidated. Allah coupled hearing with light, saying ﴿Will you not listen?﴾, because hearing perceives what sight does not, namely the recognition of its benefits and the description of its advantages. He coupled sight with night, saying ﴿Will you not see?﴾, because sight perceives what hearing does not regarding that.

﴿And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest in it﴾, that is, in the night, ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾, that is, in the day, through striving in gainful work, ﴿and perhaps you will be grateful﴾, that is, so that you may give thanks for Allah's favour upon you. This verse is an example of *lafʿ wa-nashr* (a rhetorical device in which two items are mentioned and then each is matched with its counterpart without specification), as in the words of Imru' al-Qays:

*"As if the hearts of the birds, moist and dry, beside their nests were the red jujube and the decayed date-stalk."*

Know that although resting during the day is possible, and seeking provision at night is also possible, namely when the moon rises over the earth, or when one is illuminated by something that gives light, such as a lamp, that is rare and uncommon and contrary to what people are accustomed to, so it is not to be taken into consideration.

﴿And the day He calls them and says: "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ Allah repeated this because the two states differ: they are called once, and they call upon the idols, and they are called another time and they fall silent. In this repetition there is also rebuke upon rebuke and reproach upon reproach.

His saying ﴿And We will extract from every nation a witness﴾ is coordinated with "He calls." It came in the past tense to indicate certainty. The meaning is: We will bring forth from every nation among the nations a witness who will testify against them.

Mujahid said: they are the prophets. It is also said: the upright ones of every nation. The first view is preferable. Similar is His saying: ﴿How then, when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾ (al-Nisa' 4:41). Then Allah explains what He will say to every one of these nations, in His saying: ﴿Then We will say: "Produce your proof"﴾, that is, your argument and evidence that I have partners. At that point they confess and are struck dumb, unable to establish proof. Therefore He said: ﴿Then they will know that the truth belongs to Allah﴾ in divinity, and that He alone has no partner, ﴿and what they used to fabricate will be lost to them﴾, that is, what they used to invent of falsehood in this world, namely that Allah has partners who deserve worship, will disappear, vanish and be gone.

Then Allah follows the account of the people of misguidance with the story of Qarun, because of what it contains of wondrous power and marvellous creation. He said: ﴿Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses﴾. *Qarun* is on the pattern of *fa'ul* and is a non-Arabic proper noun, which is not inflected because of its foreignness and its being a proper name. It is not an Arabic word derived from *qaranta* (to bind).

Al-Zajjaj said: if Qarun were derived from *qaranta al-shay'* (to join a thing), it would take nunation (tanwin).

Al-Nakha'i, Qatada and others said: he was the paternal cousin of Moses, namely Qarun son of Yashar son of Qahith son of Lawi son of Ya'qub, and Moses is the son of 'Imran son of Qahith.

Ibn Ishaq said: he was the paternal uncle of Moses, full brother of his father and mother; he made him a brother of 'Imran, and both were sons of Qahith. It is also said he was the maternal cousin of Moses. There was no one among the Children of Israel who knew the Torah better than him. He then became a hypocrite, as the Samiri did, and departed from obedience to Moses. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So he oppressed them﴾, that is, he exceeded the limit in arrogance and haughtiness towards them, went out against them, departed from Moses' obedience and disbelieved in Allah.

Al-Dahhak said: his oppression of the Children of Israel was his belittling them because of his abundance of wealth and children.

Qatada said: his oppression was attributing what Allah had given him of wealth to himself, due to his knowledge and cleverness.

It is also said that he was an official of Pharaoh over the Children of Israel, and he transgressed against them and wronged them. It is also said that his oppression was other than this, but that does not fit the meaning of the verse.

﴿And We gave him of the treasures﴾, the plural of *kanz* (treasure), which is wealth that is stored up.

'Ata' said: he came upon a treasure from the treasures of Joseph. It is also said that he practised *al-kimiya'* (alchemy).

In His saying ﴿Indeed, its keys﴾, *ma* is a relative pronoun whose clause is *inna* together with what is within its domain, and for this reason *inna* is pronounced with a kasra.

Al-Akhfash al-Saghir transmitted from the Kufans that they prohibited making the clause introduced by *inna* with a kasra and what is within its domain a relative clause of *alladhi*. He considered this an abomination on their part, because it occurs in the Mighty Book in this very place.

*Mafatih* is the plural of *miftah* with a kasra on the *mim*, which is that by which something is opened. It is also said that the intended meaning of *mafatih* is the storehouses, in which case its singular is *mafta*h with a fatha on the *mim*.

Al-Wahidi said: most of the exegetes hold that *mafatih* means the storehouses, as in His saying: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen﴾ (al-An'am 6:59). He said: this is the view chosen by al-Zajjaj, for he said: the more likely interpretation is that its keys are the storehouses of his wealth.

Others said: they are the plural of *miftah*, which is that by which a door is opened. This is the view of Qatada and Mujahid.

﴿Would bend the group of strong men﴾. This clause is the predicate of *inna*, and *inna* together with its subject and predicate forms the relative clause of *ma*. It is said: *na'a bi-hamlihi* means he rose up with it heavily laden; and *na'a bi-l-hamlu* means the load weighed him down. The meaning is that the burden of the keys weighs them down.

Abu 'Ubayda said: this is an inverted usage, and the meaning is: the group rises up with them, that is, stands up with them.

Abu Zayd said: *nu'tu bi-l-hamli* means that you rose up with the load. The poet said:

*"We found a successor, most wretched successor, a servant who, when he rises with the load, stands still."*

Al-Farra' said: the meaning of *tanu'u bi-l-'usbah* is that it inclines them with its weight, as one says: *yadhhabu bi-l-bu'si* and *yadhhabu al-bu's* (he takes away the misery), *dhahabtu bihi* and *adhhabtuhu* (I went with it and I made it go), *ji'tu bihi* and *aja'tuhu* (I brought it and I made it come), *nu'tu bihi* and *an'atuhu* (I raised it and I made it rise). Al-Nahhas chose this view, and many of the *salaf* (the earliest generations of Muslims) said likewise.

It is also said that it is derived from *al-na'y* (distance), but this is far-fetched.

Budayl ibn Maysara read *li-yanu'a* with a *ya'*, meaning: so that one of them, or the one mentioned, would bend under it. It was taken in this sense. The group (*'usbah*) is a company whose members support one another. It is said it is from three to ten; it is also said from ten to fifteen; it is said between ten and twenty; it is said from five to ten; it is said forty; it is said seventy; and it is said other than this.

﴿When his people said to him: "Do not exult"﴾. The adverbial clause is in the accusative governed by *tanu'u*. It is also said it is governed by *atayna-hu*, and also by *baghā*.

Abu Hayyan rejected both, on the ground that the giving and the transgression did not occur at that time.

Ibn Jarir said: it is connected to an elided verb, which is *udhkur* (remember), and the intended "his people" here are the believers from the Children of Israel.

Al-Farra' said: it is Moses, and it is a plural used for the singular. The meaning of "do not exult" is: do not be insolent or arrogant. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the exultant﴾, the insolent and arrogant, who do not thank Allah for what He has given them.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: do not exult in wealth, for one who exults in wealth does not fulfil its right. It is also said the meaning is: do not corrupt, as in the words of the poet:

*"If you do not cease to discharge a trust, and then bear another, the deposits will make you exult."*

That is: they will corrupt you. Al-Zajjaj said: *al-farihin* and *al-farihin* are equivalent. Al-Farra' said: *al-farihin* are those who are in a state of exultation, and *al-farihin* are those who will exult in the future.

Mujahid said: the meaning of "do not exult" is "do not transgress," and "Allah does not love the exultant" means the transgressors.

It is also said that it means: do not be miserly, for Allah does not love the miserly.

﴿And seek, in what Allah has given you, the Hereafter abode﴾, that is: seek, through the wealth Allah has given you, the Hereafter abode, so spend it in what pleases Allah, not in arrogance and transgression. It has been read as *wa-ittabi'* (and follow).

﴿And do not forget your share of this world﴾. The majority of exegetes said: this means that one should work in one's worldly life for the sake of the Hereafter, and a person's share is his lifespan and his righteous deeds.

Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is: do not forget to work for your Hereafter, because the reality of a person's share of this world is that through which he works for his Hereafter.

Al-Hasan and Qatada said: its meaning is: do not neglect your portion of your worldly life in enjoying what is lawful and seeking it. This is closer to the sense of the Qur'anic wording.

﴿And do good as Allah has done good to you﴾, that is, do good to the servants of Allah as Allah has done good to you by the blessings of this world with which He has favoured you. It is also said: obey Allah and worship Him as He has favoured you. This is supported by what is established in the *Sahihayn* (the two *Sahih* collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim) and others, that Gabriel asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about *ihsan* (excellence), and he said: "That you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, He sees you."

﴿And do not seek corruption in the earth﴾, that is, do not act in it with the disobedience of Allah. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the corrupters﴾ in the earth.

﴿He said: "I was only given it on knowledge I have"﴾. Qarun said this statement in reply to those who advised him with what has preceded. That is: I was only given the wealth I was given because of my knowledge. So his saying *'ala 'ilm* (on knowledge) is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause, and *'indi* (with me) is either an adverb of place for *ufitituhu* (I was given it), or a complement to *'ilm* (knowledge). This knowledge is what he made the cause of what he obtained of this world.

It is said: it is knowledge of the Torah. It is said: it is his knowledge of the ways of earning and trade. It is said: it is knowledge of the knowledge of treasures and hidden stores. It is said: it is the knowledge of alchemy. It is said: the meaning is that Allah gave me these treasures with knowledge from Him of my worthiness for them, because of the excellence of His knowledge of me.

Al-Zajjaj chose this view and rejected all others.

Then Allah refuted his statement, saying: ﴿Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him generations who were greater than him in strength and more abundant in accumulation?﴾ The *qurun* (generations) are the former nations. The meaning of "more abundant in accumulation" is: more abundant than him in gathering wealth. Had wealth or strength indicated excellence, Allah would not have destroyed them.

It is also said: *quwwah* (strength) refers to instruments, and *jam'* (accumulation) refers to helpers.

This statement is in the form of rebuke and reproach directed at Qarun, because he had read the Torah and knew the knowledge of the earlier generations and how Allah, the Glorified, destroyed them.

﴿And the guilty will not be asked about their sins﴾, that is, they will not be asked in a manner of seeking to be pleased, as in His saying: ﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends﴾ (al-Nahl 16:84; al-Rum 30:57), ﴿So they will not be among those who are made to make amends﴾ (Fussilat 41:24). They will only be asked in a manner of rebuke and reproach, as in His saying: ﴿By your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ (al-Hijr 15:92).

Mujahid said: the angels will not ask tomorrow about the guilty, because they will be recognised by their marks, for they will be gathered with black faces and blue eyes.

Qatada said: the guilty will not be asked about their sins because they are apparent and numerous, but they will enter the Fire.

It is also said: the guilty of this nation will not be asked about the sins of the former nations.

﴿So he went out to his people in his adornment.﴾ The *fa'* (فَ) is conjunctive, linking to "[He] said" (قالَ) earlier, with the intervening material being a parenthetical insertion (*i'tiraD*, an interjected clause). The phrase ﴿in his adornment﴾ (فِي زِينَتِهِ) is connected either to "went out" (خَرَجَ) or to an omitted verb, and it functions as a circumstantial qualifier (*hal*) of the subject of "went out."

The exegetes have transmitted various reports about the adornment in which he went out, but the meaning is that he went out in a display that dazzled everyone who saw it. For this reason, those who observed him wished that they too had the like of it, as God relates about them when He says: ﴿Those who desired the life of this world and its adornment said, "Would that we had the like of what Qarun was given! Indeed, he is possessed of great fortune."﴾ That is, a abundant share of worldly goods.

The exegetes differ regarding who these people were who spoke this statement. It has been said that they were believers of that time, and it has been said that they were a group of disbelievers.

﴿But those who had been given knowledge said﴾, and they were the rabbis (*ahbar*) of the Children of Israel, they said to those who had wished: ﴿Woe to you! The reward of God is better﴾, that is, God's reward in the Hereafter is better than what you wish for, ﴿for those who believe and do righteous deeds.﴾ So do not wish for the fleeting goods of this world, which do not endure. ﴿But none receives it except the patient﴾, that is, this word which the rabbis spoke. It has been said that the pronoun refers to the righteous deeds, and it has been said that it refers to Paradise. ﴿Except the steadfast﴾ in obedience to God, and those who restrain themselves from desires.

﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾. It is said: "The place sank (*khasafa*) and sinks (*yakhsifu*), sinking (*khusuufan*)": it went down into the earth. And "He caused the earth to swallow him (*khasafa bihi al-ard*), swallowing (*khasfan*)": that is, he disappeared into it. The meaning is that God, glorified is He, made him disappear and made his home disappear into the earth. ﴿So he had no company to help him against God, nor was he among those who could defend himself﴾: that is, he had no group who could ward this off from him, nor was he himself among those who could protect himself against the sinking that had befallen him.

﴿And those who had wished to be in his place yesterday began to say﴾, that is, in the recent past, ﴿"Ah! It is God who expands provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it. Had God not been gracious to us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us! Ah! The disbelievers will never prosper."﴾ That is, each of them said, regretting what had escaped from him of wishing.

An-Nahhas said: "The best that has been said about this is what al-Khalil, Sibawayh, Yunus and al-Kisa'i said: that the people became alert and said *way* (وَيْ). The one who regrets among the Arabs says *way* in the midst of his remorse." Al-Jawhari said: "*Way* (وَيْ) is an expression of wonder. It is also said *waykа* (وَيْكَ), and *way* may enter upon *ka'anna* (كَأنَّ), both the light and the heavy forms: *waykaʾanna Allah* (وَيْكَأنَّ اللَّهَ)." Al-Khalil said: "It is separated: you say *way*, then you begin and say *ka'anna*." Al-Farra' said: "It is a word of affirmation, like your saying: *Do you not see God's handiwork and His kindness?*" It has also been said: "It is a word of alerting, equivalent to *ala* (أَلا)." Qutrub said: "It is originally *wayka* (وَيْكَ), and its *lam* (لام) was dropped," and from it is the saying of 'Antarah:

*And indeed he has healed my soul and cured its ailment: the saying of the horsemen, "Wayka, 'Antar, advance!"*

Ibn al-A'rabi said: the meaning of *waykaʾanna Allah* is: "I know that God..." Al-Qutabi said: its meaning in the dialect of Himyar is "mercy." It has also been said: it means "Did you not see?" It is reported from al-Kisa'i that he said: it is an expression of grief.

﴿Had God not been gracious to us﴾ with His mercy and preserved us from the like of what Qarun had been upon, of insolence and transgression, and had not taken us to account for what had occurred from us of that wishing, ﴿He would have caused the earth to swallow us﴾ just as He caused it to swallow him.

Hafs read *la-khasafa* (لَخَسَفَ) with the active verb, while the rest read it in the passive. ﴿Ah! The disbelievers will never prosper﴾, that is, they will not attain any of their aims.

﴿That is the Last Abode﴾, that is, Paradise. The pointing to it is for the purpose of exalting it and magnifying its status, as if He said: "That which you have heard of and whose matter has reached you." ﴿We appoint it for those who do not desire exaltation in the earth﴾, that is, rising and arrogance over the believers, ﴿nor corruption﴾, that is, acting in disobedience to God, glorified is He. The mention of exaltation and corruption as indefinite nouns within a negative context indicates that both are general, covering everything to which the term "exaltation" or "corruption" applies, without restriction to any particular type. As for corruption, it is clear that no part of it is permitted, whatever it may be. As for exaltation, what is prohibited is that which is by way of arrogance toward others and haughtiness over people. Excluded from this is the pursuit of elevation in the truth and leadership in religion, nor the love of fine clothing, fine mount, or fine dwelling.

﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it﴾, and that is that God rewards him tenfold, up to seven hundredfold. ﴿And whoever brings an evil deed, those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed except according to what they used to do.﴾ That is, except the like of what they used to do; the genitive complement has been omitted and the complement after it has been put in its place. The explanation of the meaning of this verse has already been given in Surat al-Naml.

﴿Indeed, He who ordained the Qur'an upon you﴾. The exegetes said: that is, He revealed the Qur'an to you. Al-Zajjaj said: He imposed upon you the obligation to act in accordance with what the Qur'an requires, and the sense of the statement is: He imposed upon you the rulings and obligations of the Qur'an. ﴿Will surely bring you back to a return (*ma'ad*).﴾ The majority of exegetes said: that is, to Mecca.

Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Zuhri and al-Hasan said: the meaning is: "He will surely bring you back to the Day of Resurrection," and this is the choice of al-Zajjaj. It is said: "Between me and you is the *ma'ad*," that is, the Day of Resurrection, because people return (*ya'uduna*) in it alive.

Abu Malik and Abu Salih said: "He will surely bring you back to a return," that is, to Paradise. This was also said by Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and it is reported from Mujahid.

It has also been said: *ma'ad* means death. ﴿Say, "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance and who is in clear error."﴾ This is an answer to the disbelievers of Mecca when they said to the Prophet (ﷺ), "You are in error." The intended meaning of "who has come with guidance" is the Prophet (ﷺ), and "who is in clear error" refers to the polytheists. The more appropriate reading of the verse is that it is general: God, glorified is He, knows the condition of each of these two groups and will recompense each according to what it deserves of good or evil.

﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be cast to you﴾, that is, you did not expect that We would send you to the servants and reveal the Qur'an to you. It has also been said: you did not expect that the Book would be cast to you except by your being returned to your *ma'ad*. The exception in His words ﴿except as a mercy from your Lord﴾ is disjunctive (*munqati'*), that is, "but its being cast to you is a mercy from your Lord." It is also permissible for it to be connected (*muttasil*), by taking it according to the sense, as if it were said: "The Book was not cast to you except for the sake of mercy from your Lord." The first is preferable, and al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' affirmed it.

﴿So never be an aide to the disbelievers﴾, that is, a supporter for them. This contains an allusion to others among the community. It has also been said: the intended meaning is, do not be a supporter for them by flattering them.

﴿And let them not averted you from the signs of God after they have been revealed to you﴾, that is: O Muhammad, let not the disbelievers, their statements, their lies, and their harm, turn you away from reciting the signs of God and acting upon them after God has revealed them to you and they have been made obligatory upon you.

The majority read *yasuddannaka* (يَصُدَّنَّكَ) with a fathah on the *ya'* and a dammah on the *sad*, from *sadda, yasuddu*. 'Asim read it with a dammah on the *ya'* and a kasrah on the *sad*, from *asadda*, with the same meaning as *saddaha*. ﴿And call to your Lord﴾, that is, call people to God and to His oneness, to acting upon His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions. ﴿And do not be among the polytheists﴾. This also contains an allusion to others, as mentioned earlier, since he (ﷺ) would never be among the polytheists under any circumstances.

Likewise His words: ﴿And do not invoke with God another deity﴾, for it is an allusion to others.

Then He, glorified is He, singled Himself out and described Himself as enduring and everlasting, saying: ﴿There is no deity except Him. Everything will perish except His Face﴾, that is, except His Essence, of all things, whatever they may be.

Al-Zajjaj said: "*Wajhahu* (وَجْهَهُ) is in the accusative as an exception. Had it been outside the Qur'an, it would have been in the nominative, meaning: everything other than His face is perishing, as the poet said:

*And every brother, his brother will part from him, by the life of your father, except the two Pleiades (al-Farqadan)*

The meaning is: every brother other than the two Pleiades will be parted from by his brother. ***Lahu al-hukm*** (لَهُ الحُكْمُ): that is, the executing judgment; He decides what He wills and rules by what He desires, and to Him you will be returned at the Resurrection, so that He may recompense the good-doer for his goodness and the evildoer for his evil. There is no deity but Him, glorified and exalted is He.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿perpetual (*sarmadan*)﴾ that he said: "Continuous."

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him regarding ﴿and what they used to invent (*yaftarun*) will be lost to them﴾ on the Day of Resurrection that he said: "They used to lie in the world."

Ibn Abi Shaybah in *al-Musannaf*, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh reported from him as well regarding ﴿Indeed, Qarun was of the people of Moses﴾ that he said: "He was his paternal cousin, and he pursued knowledge until he gathered a body of knowledge. He continued in this matter until he rebelled against Moses and envied him. Moses said to him, 'God has commanded me to take the zakat.' He refused and said, 'Moses wants to eat up your wealth. He brought you prayer and brought you things, and you bore them. Will you bear giving him your wealth?' They said, 'We will not bear it. So what do you suggest?' He said to them, 'I suggest that we send to a prostitute among the prostitutes of the Children of Israel and send her to him, so that she accuses him of having wanted her for herself.' They sent to her and said, 'We will give you your reward on condition that you testify against Moses that he committed adultery with you.' She said, 'Yes.' Then Qarun came to Moses and said, 'Gather the Children of Israel and inform them of what your Lord has commanded you.' He said, 'Yes.' So he gathered them, and they said to him, 'What has your Lord commanded you?' He said, 'He commanded me that you worship God and associate nothing with Him, and that you maintain the ties of kinship, such and such.' And He commanded me that if someone commits adultery after being married, he should be stoned.' They said, 'Even if you are the one?' He said, 'Yes.' They said, 'You have committed adultery.' He said, 'I?' They sent for the woman, and she came. They said, 'What do you testify concerning Moses?' Moses said to her, 'I adjure you by God, speak the truth!' She said, 'As for when you adjure me by God, they called me and offered me a payment on condition that I accuse you with myself, while I testify that you are innocent and that you are the Messenger of God.' Moses fell down in prostration weeping. God revealed to him, 'What makes you weep? We have empowered you over the earth, so command it and it will obey you.' He raised his head and said, 'Seize them.' It seized them up to their ankles, and they began to say, 'O Moses, O Moses!' He said, 'Seize them.' It seized them up to their knees, and they began to say, 'O Moses, O Moses!' He said, 'Seize them.' It seized them up to their necks, and they began to say, 'O Moses, O Moses!' He said, 'Seize them.' It seized them and engulfed them. God revealed, 'O Moses, My servants asked you and humbled themselves before you, and you did not respond to them. By My might, had they called upon Me, I would have responded to them.'"

Ibn 'Abbas said: "That is His saying: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾. He was swallowed down into the lowest earth."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Khaythamah that he said: "The keys to the treasures of Qarun were made of hide, each key like a finger. Each key was for a separate treasure-house. When he rode, the keys were carried on seventy white-blazed mules."

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir reported from him: "I found in the Gospel that the mules bearing the keys to the treasuries of Qarun were white-blazed, and no key of them exceeded a finger in size, each key for a treasure."

I say: I have not found in the Gospel what Khaythamah mentioned.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿would weigh down with the band﴾ that he said: "It burdens." And Ibn al-Mundhir reported from him that he said: "The band (*'usbah*) of men of strength could not lift them." Ibn Jarir also reported from him: "The *'usbah* is forty men."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him also regarding His words ﴿Indeed, God does not love the exultant﴾ that he said: "The insolent (*maridin*)." And regarding His words ﴿And do not forget your share of the world﴾ he said: "That you work in it for your Hereafter."

Ibn Mardawayh reported from Aws ibn Aws al-Thaqafi, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His words ﴿So he went out to his people in his adornment﴾: "With four thousand mules."

Reports have been transmitted from a group of the Successors (*tabi'un*) concerning the statements explaining what he went out with to his people in adornment, but none of them is authentic as a hadith traced to the Prophet. Rather, they are from the reports of the People of the Book, as we have made clear to you more than once. I do not know the chain (*isnad*) of this hadith which Ibn Mardawayh traced to the Prophet, so whoever finds his book, let him examine it.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 28, verse 71–88 (part 3 of 3):

Al-Firyabi narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾. He said: He was made to sink into the lowest earth.

Al-Mahamili and al-Daylami, in Musnad al-Firdaws, narrated from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), regarding His saying: ﴿That is the abode of the Hereafter. We assign it to those who do not desire haughtiness upon the earth or corruption﴾. He said: "Arrogance upon the earth and taking by other than the truth."

A similar report is narrated from Muslim al-Bitin, Ibn Jurayj and ʿIkrimah.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Saʿid ibn Jubayr regarding ﴿who do not desire haughtiness upon the earth﴾: He said: Transgression upon the earth.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Hasan, who said: It is nobility and superiority in the eyes of those who hold authority over them.

I say: If that is for the sake of strengthening oneself through it in the cause of the truth, then it is one of the qualities of good, not one of the qualities of evil.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, who said: "Indeed, a man may love that the thong of his sandal be better than the thong of his companion's sandal, and so he enters into this verse: ﴿That is the abode of the Hereafter. We assign it to those who do not desire haughtiness upon the earth or corruption﴾."

Ibn Kathir, in his Tafsir, after mentioning this report from ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him), said: This is to be understood as referring to one who loves that out of pride, not merely for beautification; as for the latter, there is no harm in it, for it is established that "a man said: O Messenger of Allah, I love that my garment be fine and my sandal be fine. Is that from pride? He said: No. Indeed Allah is Beautiful and loves beauty."

Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn ʿAsakir narrated from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib that he said: This verse, namely ﴿That is the abode of the Hereafter﴾ etc., was revealed concerning people of justice and humility among the rulers, and among those with power from the rest of the people.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar report from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from ʿAdi ibn Hatim, who said: "When he entered upon the Prophet (ﷺ), he threw to him a cushion, but he sat on the ground and said: I bear witness that you do not seek haughtiness upon the earth or corruption. So he embraced Islam."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Dahhak.

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from ʿAli ibn al-Husayn ibn Waqid that His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, He who has ordained the Qur'an upon you﴾ — the verse — "was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at al-Juhfah when the Prophet (ﷺ) departed as an emigrant to Madinah."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated through several chains from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿Surely He who ordained the Qur'an upon you will return you to a place of return﴾. He said: To Makkah. Ibn Mardawayh added: "As He brought you out from it."

Al-Firyabi, ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri regarding ﴿will return you to a place of return﴾: He said: The Hereafter.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Bukhari in his Tarikh, Abu Yaʿla and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him also, regarding His saying: ﴿will return you to a place of return﴾: He said: Its return is Paradise; and in another wording: its return is its Hereafter.

al-Hakim in al-Tarikh and al-Daylami narrated from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, who said: ﴿will return you to a place of return﴾: Paradise.

Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar report from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him, who said: When the verse ﴿Everyone upon it will perish﴾ [al-Rahman: 26] was revealed, the angels said: The people of the earth have perished. When the verse ﴿Every soul will taste death﴾ [Al ʿImran: 185] was revealed, the angels said: Every soul has perished. When the verse ﴿Everything will perish except His Face﴾ was revealed, the angels said: The people of the heavens and the earth have perished.

ʿAbd ibn Humayd narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding ﴿Everything will perish except His Face﴾: He said: Except what is intended by His Face.

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (*Fath al-Qadir*) on Surah 28, verses 71–88 (part 1 of 3)**

Allah says: ﴿Say: "Tell me, if Allah made the night perpetual over you"﴾, meaning: inform me. *Sarmad* (perpetual, continuous) comes from *al-sard* (succession, continuity), and the *mim* is extra. Tarafa said:

*"By your life, my affair is not a cloud over you, neither my day nor my night is perpetually over you."*

It is also said that the *mim* is original, and its form is *fa'lal*, not *fa'mal*, and this is the more apparent view. Allah explains that He has prepared for them the means of livelihood so that they may give thanks for the blessing. If the age in which they live were a night that lasted until the Day of Resurrection, they would not be able to move about in it and seek what they must have of food, drink and clothing, which sustain life. Then He reminds them of His favour, saying: ﴿Who is a god other than Allah who could bring you light?﴾, meaning: is there among the gods you worship one that can lift this lasting darkness from you by means of *diya'* (light), that is, by a light in which you seek your livelihood, see what you need, have your fruits ripen, have your crops grow, and have your animals live? ﴿Will you not then listen?﴾, that is, listen with understanding, acceptance, reflection and contemplation.

Then, having finished reminding them of the favour of day, He reminds them of the favour of night, saying: ﴿Say: "Tell me, if Allah made the day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection"﴾, meaning: He made the whole age in which you live a day until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Who is a god other than Allah who could bring you a night in which you may rest?﴾, that is, in which you settle from weariness and fatigue and rest from the toil of seeking livelihood and earning. ﴿Will you not then see?﴾, that is, see this great benefit with the sight of one who takes heed and is awake, so that you may desist from what you are engaged in, namely the worship of other than Allah. When they acknowledge that none can do this except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, the proof is established against them and the doubtful arguments they cling to are invalidated. Allah coupled hearing with light, saying ﴿Will you not listen?﴾, because hearing perceives what sight does not, namely the recognition of its benefits and the description of its advantages. He coupled sight with night, saying ﴿Will you not see?﴾, because sight perceives what hearing does not regarding that.

﴿And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest in it﴾, that is, in the night, ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾, that is, in the day, through striving in gainful work, ﴿and perhaps you will be grateful﴾, that is, so that you may give thanks for Allah's favour upon you. This verse is an example of *lafʿ wa-nashr* (a rhetorical device in which two items are mentioned and then each is matched with its counterpart without specification), as in the words of Imru' al-Qays:

*"As if the hearts of the birds, moist and dry, beside their nests were the red jujube and the decayed date-stalk."*

Know that although resting during the day is possible, and seeking provision at night is also possible, namely when the moon rises over the earth, or when one is illuminated by something that gives light, such as a lamp, that is rare and uncommon and contrary to what people are accustomed to, so it is not to be taken into consideration.

﴿And the day He calls them and says: "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ Allah repeated this because the two states differ: they are called once, and they call upon the idols, and they are called another time and they fall silent. In this repetition there is also rebuke upon rebuke and reproach upon reproach.

His saying ﴿And We will extract from every nation a witness﴾ is coordinated with "He calls." It came in the past tense to indicate certainty. The meaning is: We will bring forth from every nation among the nations a witness who will testify against them.

Mujahid said: they are the prophets. It is also said: the upright ones of every nation. The first view is preferable. Similar is His saying: ﴿How then, when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾ (al-Nisa' 4:41). Then Allah explains what He will say to every one of these nations, in His saying: ﴿Then We will say: "Produce your proof"﴾, that is, your argument and evidence that I have partners. At that point they confess and are struck dumb, unable to establish proof. Therefore He said: ﴿Then they will know that the truth belongs to Allah﴾ in divinity, and that He alone has no partner, ﴿and what they used to fabricate will be lost to them﴾, that is, what they used to invent of falsehood in this world, namely that Allah has partners who deserve worship, will disappear, vanish and be gone.

Then Allah follows the account of the people of misguidance with the story of Qarun, because of what it contains of wondrous power and marvellous creation. He said: ﴿Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses﴾. *Qarun* is on the pattern of *fa'ul* and is a non-Arabic proper noun, which is not inflected because of its foreignness and its being a proper name. It is not an Arabic word derived from *qaranta* (to bind).

Al-Zajjaj said: if Qarun were derived from *qaranta al-shay'* (to join a thing), it would take nunation (tanwin).

Al-Nakha'i, Qatada and others said: he was the paternal cousin of Moses, namely Qarun son of Yashar son of Qahith son of Lawi son of Ya'qub, and Moses is the son of 'Imran son of Qahith.

Ibn Ishaq said: he was the paternal uncle of Moses, full brother of his father and mother; he made him a brother of 'Imran, and both were sons of Qahith. It is also said he was the maternal cousin of Moses. There was no one among the Children of Israel who knew the Torah better than him. He then became a hypocrite, as the Samiri did, and departed from obedience to Moses. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So he oppressed them﴾, that is, he exceeded the limit in arrogance and haughtiness towards them, went out against them, departed from Moses' obedience and disbelieved in Allah.

Al-Dahhak said: his oppression of the Children of Israel was his belittling them because of his abundance of wealth and children.

Qatada said: his oppression was attributing what Allah had given him of wealth to himself, due to his knowledge and cleverness.

It is also said that he was an official of Pharaoh over the Children of Israel, and he transgressed against them and wronged them. It is also said that his oppression was other than this, but that does not fit the meaning of the verse.

﴿And We gave him of the treasures﴾, the plural of *kanz* (treasure), which is wealth that is stored up.

'Ata' said: he came upon a treasure from the treasures of Joseph. It is also said that he practised *al-kimiya'* (alchemy).

In His saying ﴿Indeed, its keys﴾, *ma* is a relative pronoun whose clause is *inna* together with what is within its domain, and for this reason *inna* is pronounced with a kasra.

Al-Akhfash al-Saghir transmitted from the Kufans that they prohibited making the clause introduced by *inna* with a kasra and what is within its domain a relative clause of *alladhi*. He considered this an abomination on their part, because it occurs in the Mighty Book in this very place.

*Mafatih* is the plural of *miftah* with a kasra on the *mim*, which is that by which something is opened. It is also said that the intended meaning of *mafatih* is the storehouses, in which case its singular is *mafta*h with a fatha on the *mim*.

Al-Wahidi said: most of the exegetes hold that *mafatih* means the storehouses, as in His saying: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen﴾ (al-An'am 6:59). He said: this is the view chosen by al-Zajjaj, for he said: the more likely interpretation is that its keys are the storehouses of his wealth.

Others said: they are the plural of *miftah*, which is that by which a door is opened. This is the view of Qatada and Mujahid.

﴿Would bend the group of strong men﴾. This clause is the predicate of *inna*, and *inna* together with its subject and predicate forms the relative clause of *ma*. It is said: *na'a bi-hamlihi* means he rose up with it heavily laden; and *na'a bi-l-hamlu* means the load weighed him down. The meaning is that the burden of the keys weighs them down.

Abu 'Ubayda said: this is an inverted usage, and the meaning is: the group rises up with them, that is, stands up with them.

Abu Zayd said: *nu'tu bi-l-hamli* means that you rose up with the load. The poet said:

*"We found a successor, most wretched successor, a servant who, when he rises with the load, stands still."*

Al-Farra' said: the meaning of *tanu'u bi-l-'usbah* is that it inclines them with its weight, as one says: *yadhhabu bi-l-bu'si* and *yadhhabu al-bu's* (he takes away the misery), *dhahabtu bihi* and *adhhabtuhu* (I went with it and I made it go), *ji'tu bihi* and *aja'tuhu* (I brought it and I made it come), *nu'tu bihi* and *an'atuhu* (I raised it and I made it rise). Al-Nahhas chose this view, and many of the *salaf* (the earliest generations of Muslims) said likewise.

It is also said that it is derived from *al-na'y* (distance), but this is far-fetched.

Budayl ibn Maysara read *li-yanu'a* with a *ya'*, meaning: so that one of them, or the one mentioned, would bend under it. It was taken in this sense. The group (*'usbah*) is a company whose members support one another. It is said it is from three to ten; it is also said from ten to fifteen; it is said between ten and twenty; it is said from five to ten; it is said forty; it is said seventy; and it is said other than this.

﴿When his people said to him: "Do not exult"﴾. The adverbial clause is in the accusative governed by *tanu'u*. It is also said it is governed by *atayna-hu*, and also by *baghā*.

Abu Hayyan rejected both, on the ground that the giving and the transgression did not occur at that time.

Ibn Jarir said: it is connected to an elided verb, which is *udhkur* (remember), and the intended "his people" here are the believers from the Children of Israel.

Al-Farra' said: it is Moses, and it is a plural used for the singular. The meaning of "do not exult" is: do not be insolent or arrogant. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the exultant﴾, the insolent and arrogant, who do not thank Allah for what He has given them.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: do not exult in wealth, for one who exults in wealth does not fulfil its right. It is also said the meaning is: do not corrupt, as in the words of the poet:

*"If you do not cease to discharge a trust, and then bear another, the deposits will make you exult."*

That is: they will corrupt you. Al-Zajjaj said: *al-farihin* and *al-farihin* are equivalent. Al-Farra' said: *al-farihin* are those who are in a state of exultation, and *al-farihin* are those who will exult in the future.

Mujahid said: the meaning of "do not exult" is "do not transgress," and "Allah does not love the exultant" means the transgressors.

It is also said that it means: do not be miserly, for Allah does not love the miserly.

﴿And seek, in what Allah has given you, the Hereafter abode﴾, that is: seek, through the wealth Allah has given you, the Hereafter abode, so spend it in what pleases Allah, not in arrogance and transgression. It has been read as *wa-ittabi'* (and follow).

﴿And do not forget your share of this world﴾. The majority of exegetes said: this means that one should work in one's worldly life for the sake of the Hereafter, and a person's share is his lifespan and his righteous deeds.

Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is: do not forget to work for your Hereafter, because the reality of a person's share of this world is that through which he works for his Hereafter.

Al-Hasan and Qatada said: its meaning is: do not neglect your portion of your worldly life in enjoying what is lawful and seeking it. This is closer to the sense of the Qur'anic wording.

﴿And do good as Allah has done good to you﴾, that is, do good to the servants of Allah as Allah has done good to you by the blessings of this world with which He has favoured you. It is also said: obey Allah and worship Him as He has favoured you. This is supported by what is established in the *Sahihayn* (the two *Sahih* collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim) and others, that Gabriel asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about *ihsan* (excellence), and he said: "That you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, He sees you."

﴿And do not seek corruption in the earth﴾, that is, do not act in it with the disobedience of Allah. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the corrupters﴾ in the earth.

﴿He said: "I was only given it on knowledge I have"﴾. Qarun said this statement in reply to those who advised him with what has preceded. That is: I was only given the wealth I was given because of my knowledge. So his saying *'ala 'ilm* (on knowledge) is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause, and *'indi* (with me) is either an adverb of place for *ufitituhu* (I was given it), or a complement to *'ilm* (knowledge). This knowledge is what he made the cause of what he obtained of this world.

It is said: it is knowledge of the Torah. It is said: it is his knowledge of the ways of earning and trade. It is said: it is knowledge of the knowledge of treasures and hidden stores. It is said: it is the knowledge of alchemy. It is said: the meaning is that Allah gave me these treasures with knowledge from Him of my worthiness for them, because of the excellence of His knowledge of me.

Al-Zajjaj chose this view and rejected all others.

Then Allah refuted his statement, saying: ﴿Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him generations who were greater than him in strength and more abundant in accumulation?﴾ The *qurun* (generations) are the former nations. The meaning of "more abundant in accumulation" is: more abundant than him in gathering wealth. Had wealth or strength indicated excellence, Allah would not have destroyed them.

It is also said: *quwwah* (strength) refers to instruments, and *jam'* (accumulation) refers to helpers.
